Measured, honest battery budgets. Every continuous-recording figure in the category is a vendor claim, and no product shows drain measured on the user's own watch.

Languages beyond English, and records that last. Apple's features are English-only. Recap gives no full transcript, audio or export, and its summaries expire after 7 days unless saved one at a time. The EU follows only after legal review.
risks_and_open_questions: App Review may treat the audio background mode as playback-only. One developer was rejected for exactly that (forum 776949), Apple did not answer the question about long recording (forum 750432), and DTS cannot speak for App Review. This decides whether the product can exist. Mitigations: TestFlight first, Meet with Apple, user-started time-boxed Sessions, an obvious recording state, no keep-alives, and never saying 'always listening'.

Apple could widen Siri Recap and Live Rewind to older watches, more languages, the EU, transcripts or an API in any point release. No third-party API exists. On Series 12 and Ultra 4, nobody has tested whether our session and Apple's compete for the mic. The durable defences are the user-owned vault, file export, consent tooling and agent access.

Battery drain has never been measured. If real drain is near the 15-20 %/h vendors report, Series and SE users get half-day Sessions and the pitch shrinks to 'meetings only'. The recording screen appears on every wrist raise, and its cost is unmeasured. The CPU cost of SoundAnalysis and recording under Low Power Mode are also untested. Measure per model against the per-model gates in week one, before making any claim.

Interruptions cannot be recovered without a tap. Calls, Siri, alarms and apps that use audio all end capture. Heavy phone users will have many gaps and may tire of resume nudges, so real coverage could fall well short of 'a workday'. The dead-man notification catches silent deaths, but it adds one more alert.

Sync is fragile. The OS throttles transferFile, and one report describes a file under 30 MB failing. Background transfers may wait for Wi-Fi, and the network path is revoked every ~36-38 s during audio sessions (FB24377808). CloudKit uploads from a watch in a background audio session are unverified. This needs the ledger, soak tests per watch model, and tests with the iPhone's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth off.

The iPhone side is unverified. Long SpeechAnalyzer jobs may not fit within BGProcessingTask or BGContinuedProcessingTask limits, so transcripts may wait for charging or for the app to be opened. The watch shows 'Waiting for iPhone' instead of pretending, but the 'summaries never arrive' complaint could return.

Wearer separation may fail its 95% precision gate on wrist audio, since diarization is verified only on the Mac. If it fails, strict-jurisdiction Sessions without consent keep only summaries of what others said, which weakens the verifiable-record pitch in 14 states.

Wrist-mic audio quality is unknown. Pickup across a table, clothing rustle and sleeve occlusion have not been compared with multi-mic devices (Plaud Note Pro has 4 mics, Comu Action Pro 6). SpeechTranscriber's WER of 14.0 on earnings22 is a Mac benchmark, not wrist audio.

Legal exposure. Brewer v. Otter.ai and Subia v. Meta are verified, and pleading-stage rulings in early 2026 mostly favoured plaintiffs. Relevant rules: 13 all-party-consent states plus Michigan's hybrid rule, EDPB Statement 01/2026, and up to 3 years' imprisonment under §201 StGB. California's SB 1130 indicator mandate was vetoed and may return. Workplaces may ban recording. Discard and summary-only retention reduce exposure but do not cure interception claims. This is not legal advice: get counsel before an EU launch or workplace marketing.

Social rejection. A watch looks covert, and the press called Bee the 'creepiest Apple Watch app' and Siri Recap a 'passive surveillance state'. A recording screen that replaces the watch face for hours may irritate wearers. Announce through a tiny watch speaker is often inaudible, so in practice it depends on the wearer saying it. If announcing and pause zones aren't used, users drop social settings first, as the long-term Limitless user did.

Wrong attributions and hallucinations. One wrong 'you promised X' on the wrist does lasting damage, and summaries could be misused as evidence. Mitigate with citations, uncertainty labels, media filtering and a self-check before anything reaches the watch.

Pause semantics. The orange indicator stays lit while the screen says 'Paused', and bystanders may not believe it. Asking before resuming and switching to Stop after 10 unanswered minutes reduce the ambiguity. Stop must still be offered whenever someone objects.

Platform details that need device verification:
- ADTS writing on watchOS.
- Whether completeUnlessOpen lets segment writes continue after the watch locks.
- Chime playback in Silent Mode and with AirPods connected, and how .playAndRecord routes.
- Whether Double Tap and notification actions reliably bring the app forward during a background session.
- Whether the user can leave the app for the watch face during a Session.
- transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo with WidgetKit complications, and widget reload budgets.
- How coarse batteryLevel readings are, and whether volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey exists on watchOS.
- Any lock or off-wrist signal.
- AudioRecordingIntent's Live Activity requirement.
- The watchOS 26 device list for the fallback.

Cloud privacy promises depend on Anthropic confirmations. Batch ZDR eligibility is unconfirmed. The target of the server-side fallback must stay within the ZDR arrangement. The vendor's organization needs a ZDR arrangement in place. Users who bring their own key fall outside it. Until these are confirmed, the promise covers only standard Messages requests through App Attest or a stateless proxy.

Economics. Competitors offer free unlimited transcription (Pocket, Comulytic Note Pro, HiDock P1), $75 hardware with no subscription (Pebble Index 01), or a $74.99 device tied into Alexa+ (Bee Frontier). Local processing is a cost necessity, and the 4,096-token context of Foundation Models limits summary quality on the free tier.

Our own continuity. An acquisition or shutdown would repeat Limitless. Scheduled file exports, the published schema and the open-source reader mitigate this, but users who never export are exposed. The product must work locally without an account.

Evidence quality. Single-source or vendor claims: all battery figures, Chamberlain v. Granola (do not cite externally), Bee requiring a button tap after the Amazon acquisition, and wearer-only isolation in the unshipped Nirva and Taya. Sources also conflict on whether Granola keeps recording while other apps are open. Where the catalog (Nov 16) and the Earshot notes (Nov 14) disagreed, I used the catalog: Stream Ring is shipping (Earshot: preorder), and Pebble Index 01 is $75 and in stock (Earshot: $99). Catalog records marked unchecked were not re-verified.
